title: Colour contrast and non-colour cues
learningObjectives: Explain colour contrast and non-colour cues and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Text and essential visual information need sufficient contrast against their backgrounds. Colour should not be the only way to communicate status; combine it with labels, icons, patterns, or shape. Contrast should be checked for text, controls, focus indicators, and relevant graphical objects.
understand.whyItMatters: Low contrast and colour-only meaning exclude users with low vision or colour-vision differences and can fail in glare or monochrome contexts.
understand.analogy: Contrast is the difference that makes information stand out; a label adds meaning that colour alone cannot carry.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The symbols and text labels communicate status in addition to colour. Actual contrast ratios should be measured for the final palette.

practise.guidedTask: Audit a status dashboard. Measure text contrast and add text or icon cues so status is understandable without colour.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.
